answer.generated: To determine the number of processors with the highest speedup under the given conditions, we need to balance the reduction in computation time against the increase in communication overhead. Let \( n \) represent the number of processors. The speedup \( S(n) \) can be expressed as the ratio of the original execution time \( T_0 \) to the new execution time \( T(n) \), which includes both computation and communication costs. Assuming the original execution time is \( T_0 \), the new execution time for \( n \) processors is given by \( T(n) = T_{\text{comp}}(n) + T_{\text{comm}}(n) \), where \( T_{\text{comp}}(n) = \frac{T_0}{n} \) represents the computation time and \( T_{\text{comm}}(n) = \frac{0.005T_0 \cdot (n-1)}{2} \) accounts for the communication cost, considering it starts at zero when \( n=1 \) and increases by 0.5% for each additional processor. The speedup is then \( S(n) = \frac{T_0}{T_{\text{comp}}(n) + T_{\text{comm}}(n)} \). The optimal number of processors is found by maximizing \( S(n) \), typically through numerical methods or by analyzing the derivative of \( S(n) \) with respect to \( n \).
